entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.dreadcloth: A Dread Cloth is crafted with Dread Fragments, Strings and a piece of Leather.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.dreadplate: A Dreadium Plate is crafted with Dreadium Ingots and a Dread Cloth.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.dreadiumhilt: A Dreadium Katana Hilt is crafted with Dreadium Ingots, Dreadlands Wood Planks and Dread Cloth.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.dreadiumblade: A Dreadium Katana Blade is crafted with Dreadium Crystals.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.dreadiumshelm: A Dreadium Samurai Helmet is crafted with Dreadium Plates, a Dreadium Ingot and a Dreadium Helmet.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.dreadiumsplat: A Dreadium Samurai Chestplate is crafted with Dreadium Plates, Dread Cloth, a Dreadium Ingot and a Dreadium Chestplate.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.dreadiumslegs: Dreadium Samurai Leggings are crafted with Dreadium Plates, Dread Cloth and Dreadium Leggings.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.dreadiumsboot: Dreadium Boots are crafted with Dread Cloth, Dreadlands Wood Planks and Dreadium Boots.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.dreadiumkatan: A Dreadium Katana is crafted with a Dreadium Katana Blade and a Dreadium Katana Hilt.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.coraliumchunk: A Chunk of Coralium is crafted with 9-gem Coralium Clusters and an Abyssal Stone.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.coraliumplate: A Coralium Plate is crafted with Refined Coralium Ingots and Coralium Pearls.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.corhelmetp: A Plated Coralium Helmet is crafted with Coralium Pearls, Refined Coralium Ingots, Coralium Plates and a Refined Coralium Helmet.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.corplatep: A Plated Coralium Chestplate is crafted with Refined Coralium Ingots, Coralium Plates and a Refined Coralium Chestplate.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.corlegsp: Plated Coralium Leggings are crafted with Refined Coralium Ingots, Coralium Plates and Refined Coralium Leggings.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.corbootsp: Plated Coralium Boots are crafted with Refined Coralium Ingots, Coralium Plates and Refined Coralium Boots.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.corbow: A Coralium Longbow is crafted with Strings, Refined Coralium Ingots, a Coralium Pearl and a Bow.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.energypedesta: An Energy Pedestal is crafted with Monolith Stones, A Shadow Gem and a Coralium Pearl.

This block serves as a method for obtaining Potential Energy. If you place Statues 3 blocks away from it (on the x or z axis), they will transfer energy to it at a fast rate. Place a Necronomicon (or other source that can hold Potential Energy) on it in order to drain it.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.dreadium.1: Dreadium can be obtained in numerous ways. One method is to transmute Dreaded Shards of Abyssalnite (dropped by Dreadguards, Greater Dread Spawns and Lesser Dreadbeasts).
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.dreadium.2: When you have enough Dreadium Ingots to craft a Crystallizer, you can crystallize Dreaded materials to obtain Dreadium Crystals (mostly shards which you can combine into crystals that can be transmuted for Dreadium Ingots).
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.monolithpilla: A Monolith Stone Pillar is crafted with Monolith Stone. It's primary use is to amplify the range of Potential Energy Manipulators (statues for example).
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.ritualcharm.1: A Ritual Charm is crafted with Gold Ingots and a Diamond. By itself it has no effect, but through rituals it can amplify various stats of Potential Energy Manipulators.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.sacrificialal: A Sacrificial Altar is crafted with Shadow Fragments, Monolith Stone, A Shadow Gem and a Coralium Pearl. They convert life-force into Potential Energy.

When an mob is targeted, it will start glowing. Once the mob dies, an amount of PE equal to it's max health will be collected. It only targets non-undead adult mobs that aren't players. It should be noted that the altar goes on a cooldown after collecting a fifth of it's max capacity, preventing collection for a minute.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.energycollect: An Energy Collector is crafted with Monolith Stone and a Shadow Gem. They can collect PE, but require an Energy Relay to transport it.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.energyrelay: An Energy Relay is crafted with Monolith Stone, Shadow Gem Shards and a Shadow Gem. They can be used to transport PE between blocks capable of storing it.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.rendingpedest: A Rending Pedestal is crafted with Monolith Stone, A Shard of Oblivion and a Coralium Pearl. They can be used to automate the Staff of Rending.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.stonetablet: A Stone Tablet is crafted with Monolith Stone, Shadow Gem Shards and a Shadow Gem. Can be used in the State Transformer and Energy Depositioner in order to generate PE.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.statetransfor: A State Transformer is crafted with Monolith Stone, a Transmutation Gem and a Chest. It allows you to store input objects as PE in a Stone Tablet.

Fill the input slots with stacks of items, then place an empty Stone Tablet in the leftmost slot to fill it. Press the button to switch modes, allowing you to reverse the process, returning items previously stored in a Stone Tablet. The amount of PE per input item is 1 * (64/max stack size) PE/item. Input/output can be automated.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.energydeposit: An Energy Depositioner is crafted with Monolith Stone, Shadow Gems, a Transmutation Gem and an Energy Relay. This is a PE manipulator, working like statues.

By placing a charged Stone Tablet in the input slot, the Depositioner will siphon out any PE stored in it, returning either an empty Stone Tablet or a cursed one. This operation will corrupt the surrounding area (17x17 blocks), converting it into Darklands (more Darklands increases the chance of cursed Stone Tablets). Output can be automated.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.ethaxiumpilla: Ethaxium Pillars are crafted with Ethaxium Bricks and Ethaxium blocks
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.darkethaxiump: Dark Ethaxium Pillars are crafted with Dark Ethaxium Bricks and Omothol Stone
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.upgradekit.1: An Upgrade Kit is crafted with Wooden Planks, Cobblestone, String and Flint. Upgrade kits can upgrade tools and armor through an anvil.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.upgradekit.2: To upgrade a kit, you need 2 units of the next material and 1 of the current. Materials are Wood -> Cobblestone -> Iron -> Gold -> Diamond -> Abyssalnite -> Refined Coralium -> Dreadium -> Ethaxium.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.ironplate: An Iron Plate is crafted with 2 Iron Ingots. Iron Plates can enhance the saturation of certain food.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.washcloth: A Washcloth is crafted with Wool and Cobweb. It's used to clean Dirty Plates (given when eating plate food).
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.mre: An MRE (Meal, Ready to Eat) is crafted with an Iron Plate, a Carrot, a Potato and a Steak. It fills the entire food bar when eaten.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.platefood: Any Vanilla foodstuffs (and Fried Eggs) combined with an Iron Plate will create plate food (which has twice the saturation of the normal). Returns a Dirty Plate when eaten.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.odbcore: An ODB Core is crafted with Abyssalnite Ingots, Iron Ingots, Iron Blocks and a Coralium Pearl. Can be used as an explosive.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.odb: An Oblivion Deathbomb is crafted with Obsidian, An ODB Core, An Oblivion Catalyst, a Liquid Coralium Bucket and a Liquid Antimatter Bucket. Heavy explosive.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.carboncluster: A Carbon Cluster is crafted with Crystallized Carbon. They are used in order to craft Dense Carbon Clusters.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.densecarboncl: A Dense Carbon Cluster is crafted with Carbon Clusters and a block of Obsidian. Can be transmuted into a Diamond.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.crate: A Wooden Crate is crafted with Sticks, Wooden Planks and a Chest. Has an extra row of inventory slots more than a Chest.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.decorativeaza: A Decorative Azathoth Statue is crafted with Monolith Stone, Clay and Purple Dye.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.decorativecth: A Decorative Cthulhu Statue is crafted with Monolith Stone, Clay and Cyan Dye.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.decorativehas: A Decorative Hastur Statue is crafted with Monolith Stone, Clay and Dandelion Yellow.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.decorativejza: A Decorative J'zahar Statue is crafted with Monolith Stone, Clay and Gray Dye.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.decorativenya: A Decorative Nyarlathotep Statue is crafted with Monolith Stone, Clay and Lapis Lazuli.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.decorativeshu: A Decorative Shub-Niggurath Statue is crafted with Monolith Stone, Clay and an Ink Sac.
entries.necronomicon.text.crafting.decorativeyog: A Decorative Yog-Sothoth Statue is crafted with Monolith Stone, Clay and Glowstone Dust.
entries.necronomicon.text.enchantment.coralium: The Coralium Enchantment allows you to infect any entity you hit with the Coralium Plague (that is, if they aren't immune). Can only be obtained through a ritual.
entries.necronomicon.text.enchantment.dread: The Dread Enchantment allows you to infect any entity you hit with the Dread Plague (that is, if they aren't immune). Can only be obtained through a ritual.
entries.necronomicon.text.enchantment.lightpierc: The Light Pierce Enchantment works like Bane of Arthropods, but on Shadow mobs.
entries.necronomicon.text.enchantment.ironwall: The Iron Wall Enchantment works as an anti-knockback enchantment, repelling knockback applied when hit.
entries.necronomicon.text.enchantment.sapping: The Sapping Enchantment increases the amount of energy a Staff of Rending can drain.
entries.necronomicon.text.enchantment.multirend: The Multi-rend Enchantment makes the Staff of Rending also drain energy from nearby mobs within a 3 block radius of the target.
In order to reach the Abyssal Wasteland, one must craft a Gateway Key, which requires one to travel to the Nether, and to visit a Darklands and a water-based biome. The water-based biome can be either a swamp or an ocean biome.

From the Nether you need 2 Blaze Rods, and probably a few more for later. From the Darklands biome you need to slay living shadows to finally obtain Shadow Gems. They are most commonly found in Darklands Mountains biomes. It is recommended to obtain a Staff of Rending in order to obtain Shadow Gems faster (more information in the special armor and tools section).

From the water-based biome you need Coralium Gems in order to create Coralium Pearls. Once you have obtained these items, you can create a Transmutation Gem through an Infusion Ritual (found in the ritual section). The recipe for Shards of Oblivion can be found in the special materials section.

When you have 4 Shards of Oblivion, use those and 4 units of Redstone Dust to infuse an Eye of Ender (through an infusion ritual, found in the ritual section of the Necronomicon) in order to create an Oblivion Catalyst, main component of the Gateway Key (the special materials section has the recipe).

Once the Gateway Key is crafted, simply right-click on the ground to form a portal. For more information, you will need the Abyssal Wasteland Necronomicon, which requires 8 Skins of The Abyssal Wasteland in order to upgrade. The Staff of Rending is needed in order to obtain essences used to craft those.
entries.necronomicon.text.abyssal.progression.1: Once you have reached the Abyssal Wasteland, your next goal is to reach the Dreadlands. You will need 3 components in order to upgrade your Gateway Key, an Eye of The Abyss, a Dreadlands Infused Powerstone and a Transmutation Gem. The first is obtained by defeating Asorah, The Fallen, summoned through the ritual "Ritual of The Sleeper" (in ritual section).
entries.necronomicon.text.abyssal.progression.2: Asorah uses Spectral Dragons to heal himself, so they should be taken out quickly throughout the fight. Once defeated, Asorah will drop his eye with a large quantity of exp and materials found in the dimension. The Dreadlands Infused Powerstone is located inside an Abyssal Stronghold, which can be found using Powerstone Trackers (recipe in special materials section).
entries.necronomicon.text.abyssal.progression.3: Once you have tracked down the Powerstone, you can mine it with a Refined Coralium Pickaxe. Lastly you can upgrade your Gateway Key by infusing it with the required components ("Asorah's Dreaded Gateway Key" ritual). Upgrading your Necronomicon to the Dreadlands Necronomicon requires 8 Skins of The Dreadlands.
entries.necronomicon.text.dreadlands.progression: Once you have reached the Dreadlands, your next goal is to reach Omothol. You will need to own a Transmutator, and you need to defeat Cha'garoth, The Dreadbeast. In order to reach Cha'garoth, you need the Altar of Cha'garoth, made out of 2 pieces. Both pieces are created through rituals.

Once you have both Altar pieces, you need to place them at Y = 40 inside a Dreadlands Mountain biome and right-click it. Doing so will grant you entry to The Lair of Cha'garoth. After fighting through Dreadguards and eventually killing Cha'garoth, you will receive a Dread-plagued Gateway Key, along with loot. The key needs to be transmuted into a functioning one.

With the aforementioned Transmutator (recipe in Abyssal Wasteland special materials section) you can transmute the Dread-plagued Gateway Key into Cha'garoth's R'lyehian Gateway Key, granting you access to Omothol. Upgrading your Necronomicon to the Omothol Necronomicon requires 8 Skins of Omothol.
entries.necronomicon.text.omothol.progression.1: Now that you've arrived in Omothol, it's time to battle J'zahar, Gatekeeper of The Abyss. The Temple of J'zahar can be located at the heart of Omothol (coordinates X=4, Y=53, Z=7). Once you have defeated the Gatekeeper, you will be able to unlock all hidden knowledge through the Abyssalnomicon.
entries.necronomicon.text.omothol.progression.2: The Abyssalnomicon requires Ethaxium Ingots, Eldritch Scales and the Essence of The Gatekeeper (dropped by J'zahar).
Once you have reached the Dark Realm, there isn't much to do down here apart from facing infinite waves of Shadow beings and Sacthoth, as this is his natural habitant.
Main reason to intentionally fall down here would be to obtain large quantities of Shadow Gems and/or Sacthoth's Soul Reaper Blade.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.anti.1: Inside the Coralium Infested Swamp you can find several life forms made out of antimatter.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.anti.2: If an anti-entity collides with it's normal counterpart, they explode. There are anti-versions of: Zombies, Abyssal Zombies, Skeletons, Depths Ghouls, Bats, Cows, Pigs, Chickens, Creepers, Spiders and Players. Anti-Players don't explode.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.evilanimals.1: If you encounter any of these animals, you will quickly notice that it's hostile and screams when you hit it.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.evilanimals.2: The Evil Animals are pre-evolving Demon Animals, which hatches when you kill the current animal-based organism. They are immune to fire, and spawn in most Overworld biomes.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.abyssalzombie.1: Abyssal Zombies can be found in various Ocean, Swamp, Beach and Darklands biomes.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.abyssalzombie.2: Abyssal Zombies are formerly Zombies who has been infected with the Coralium Plague, causing them to evolve into these beings. They are hostile against regular Zombies. They also spawn in the Abyssal Wasteland and the End.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.depthsghoul.1: Depths Ghouls are evolved Coralium Infested undead. Spawns where Abyssal Zombies spawn.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.depthsghoul.2: Depths Ghouls are the masterpiece of Coralium Plague evolution on Zombies, rarely mutating into these behemoths. Some of them gains new forms, such as Pete, Mr. Wilson and Dr. Orange, each stronger than the other.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.skeletongoliath: Skeleton Goliaths are massive Skeletons with Cudgels roaming the Abyssal Wasteland. Unknown Origin.

Ever thought what a giant skeleton with a Cudgel would look like in Minecraft? Well, this. Skeleton Goliaths are big and powerful skeletons walking among the dead. They have a small chance of dropping the Cudgel on death.
Spectral Dragons are transparent dragons rarely spawning in the Abyssal Wasteland.

These ghastly dragons are mostly a nuisance to face, but probably more tricky when Asorah devours their life energy in order to regenerate himself. They can fly through solid matter without destroying it, unlike the Ender Dragon.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.asorah.1: Asorah, The Fallen, is the first boss encountered in AbyssalCraft. Summoned inside the Abyssal Wasteland.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.asorah.2: Asorah was formerly Oblivionaire's dragon, until he passed away aeons ago, after that he has been reanimated through the usage of Coralium until he was destroyed by an unknown enemy. Now his soul resides in the Dark Realm.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.abyssalnitegole: Abyssalnite Golems are living ore clusters found in the Dreadlands.

These creatures of solid Abyssalnite were the native population of the dimensional mine that became the Dreadlands. They tend to pick fights with their Dreaded counterpart, to avenge their lost world.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.dreadgolem.1: Dreaded Abyssalnite Golems are living ore clusters found in the Dreadlands.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.dreadgolem.2: Unlike the pure Abyssalnite Golems, these red chunks of corrupted Abyssalnite are slowly turning into Dreadium, while taking all measures on corrupting any remaining Abyssalnite.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.dreadling.1: Dreadlings are mutated beings found in the Dreadlands.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.dreadling.2: These beings were once Abyssalnite miners in the dimension that became the Dreadlands. They have no memory of their past, and now lives to worship Cha'garoth, The Dreadbeast, who controls them.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.dreadspawn.1: Dread Spawns are mutated beings found in the Dreadlands. They are rumored to share certain genetic features with Shoggoths.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.dreadspawn.2: It is not known what these beings are, but one thing is sure, Cha'garoth created them. Dread Spawns are slowly crawling mutants appearing often in Dreadlands Forests. If enough of them group up at one spot, they might merge, growing into a larger mass.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.demonanimals.1: Demon Animals are demonic monsters found in the Nether and the Dreadlands.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.demonanimals.2: These abominations are commonly found in Dreadlands Forests or randomly in the Nether. How these monsters were created is unknown, but someone hated humans enough to turn farm animals hostile against them.
Spawns of Cha'garoth are mutated beings found in the Dreadlands.

Compared to the Dread Spawn, these mutated beings are the offspring of Cha'garoth, having a few of his features. They are stronger than their lesser counterpart (the Dread Spawn), and are usually spawned by Cha'garoth.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.chagarothfist.1: Fists of Cha'garoths are living hands found in the Dreadlands.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.chagarothfist.2: As the Dreadbeast is immobile, he managed to create arms that stretched almost infinitely across the Dreadlands, with empty eyeballs for him to gaze through. This is literally a hand holding an eyeball.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.dreadguard.1: Dreadguards are powerful mutants found in the Dreadlands.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.dreadguard.2: These particular beings have been empowered by Cha'garoth, and placed in corrupted Abyssalnite Armor with the task of guarding their master, which they do quite well. They drop Dreaded Shards of Abyssalnite.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.chagaroth.1: Cha'garoth, The Dreadbeast, is the Second boss in AbyssalCraft, encountered in the Dreadlands.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.chagaroth.2: Cha'garoth is the result of a new dangerous virus, 3 chopped off hydra heads and a dead Shoggoth. Becoming a health hazard for The Great Old Ones, he was placed in the dimension that became the Dreadlands, killing and corrupting everything.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.remnant.1: Remnants are the citizens of Omothol, found there.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.remnant.2: Since all Great Old Ones has some type of offspring, J'zahar has the Remnants, whom are lesser beings of himself, incapable of obtaining the power he bears. Instead they worship him like his loyal breed, and trade goods with other life forms.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.omotholghoul.1: Omothol ghouls are the final evolution, found in Omothol.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.omotholghoul.2: The Omothol Ghoul is the final evolution of the Depths Ghoul, unlocking the full potential of death. Aeons in darkness has made these behemoths immune to fire, while strengthening them greatly.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.omotholwarden.1: Omothol Wardens are demons found in Omothol.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.omotholwarden.2: Omothol Wardens are demons tasked by J'zahar to patrol Omothol, searching for intruders to eliminate. These demonic beings are powerful guardians of the Abyss.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.gatekeeperminio: Minions of The Gatekeeper are loyal servants to J'zahar found in Omothol.
Minions of The Gatekeeper are an elite of more powerful Remnants serving their master. They are commonly found around The Temple of J'zahar, being loyal minions to the Gatekeeper.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.jzahar.1: J'zahar, Gatekeeper of The Abyss, is the final boss in AbyssalCraft, found in Omothol.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.jzahar.2: J'zahar was the only one among The Great Old Ones to not get banished to the eternal void. Due to the powers he obtained when he reverted time and space to re-create it, he is tasked with guarding his fellow demonic gods in their eternal slumber.
Lesser Shoggoths are a smaller breed of Shoggoths found throughout the Abyss.

Shoggoths are amorphous shapeshifting beings genetically engineered by the Elder Things as a race of servant-tools. Though being mindless, they became conscious and killed their masters. Now they sometimes build monoliths in honor of The Great Old Ones.
Shadow Creatures are inhabitants of The Dark Realm, can be found in Darklands Mountains.

Shadow Creatures are living shadows naturally found in The Dark Realm, but are capable of merging to Omothol and all the way to the Darklands. The Shadow Creature is the smallest evolution of living shadows.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.shadowmonster.1: Shadow Monsters are inhabitants of The Dark Realm, can be found in Darklands Mountains.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.shadowmonster.2: Shadow Monsters are living shadows naturally found in The Dark Realm, but are capable of merging to Omothol and all the way to the Darklands. The Shadow Monster is the middle evolution of living shadows.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.shadowbeast.1: Shadow Beasts are inhabitants of The Dark Realm, can be found in Darklands Mountains.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.shadowbeast.2: Shadow Beasts are living shadows naturally found in The Dark Realm, but are capable of merging to Omothol and all the way to the Darklands. The Shadow Beast is the greater evolution of living shadows.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.shadowtitan.1: Shadow Titans are inhabitants of The Dark Realm.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.shadowtitan.2: Shadow Titans are powerful living shadows roaming The Dark Realm. Compared to the Shadow Beast, Shadow Titans are armored, and more powerful.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.sacthoth.1: Sacthoth, Harbinger of Doom is found in The Dark Realm.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.sacthoth.2: Sacthoth is the strongest being in The Dark Realm, and the ruler of living shadows. The only way for him to leave The Dark Realm is through the explosion of an Oblivion Deathbomb. He carries a powerful sword capable of tearing out the souls of the living.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.coraliumsquid.1: Coralium Infested Squids are found in pools of Liquid Coralium inside the Abyssal Wasteland.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.coraliumsquid.2: These Squids have been transformed by the Coralium Plague, enabling them to transfer it to victims touched by them, or the ink they squirt on their targets.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.shuboffspring.1: Dark Offspring are vile beasts resembling a goat mixed with a dead tree, and are the offspring of Shub-Niggurath.
entries.necronomicon.text.entity.shuboffspring.2: These beasts can rarely be found in forests (most common in Roofed Forests and Darklands Forests). You know you're getting close to one if you start hearing sheep out of nowhere. You're most likely to encounter one at night during a new moon.
entries.necronomicon.text.rituals.info: Check the information section for information regarding rituals, or the other sections for information about available rituals. "Location" specifies where the ritual can be performed.
entries.necronomicon.text.rituals.1: In order to get started with rituals you need to create the altar to perform them at. There is a total of 8 materials you can create your Ritual Altar from.
entries.necronomicon.text.rituals.2: Those are: Cobblestone, Darkstone Cobblestone, Abyssal Cobblestone, Coralium Cobblestone, Dreadstone Cobblestone, Abyssalnite Cobblestone, Ethaxium Brick and Dark Ethaxium Brick. The materials can only be used in their specific dimension (eg. Cobblestone and Darkstone Cobblestone in the Overworld, Abyssal Cobblestone in the Abyssal Wasteland etc).
entries.necronomicon.text.rituals.3: To create the altar, simply place the blocks in the above formation (keep the colored area clear) and shift right-click the center block with a Necronomicon.
entries.necronomicon.text.rituals.4: After that, you can start performing rituals! In order to perform a ritual, place objects on the pedestals and shift right-click the altar with a Necronomicon.
entries.necronomicon.text.rituals.5: When performing, the pedestals project bits of their placed object towards the altar. Rituals where you gain objects always end with a bolt of lightning striking the altar.
entries.necronomicon.text.rituals.6: Potential Energy is required in order to perform rituals (each ritual entry shows how much you need). Potential Energy is a pure form of untapped energy originating from a higher plane of existence. It's mainly used to fuel sacrifices made to The Great Old Ones (any ritual). Statues placed on Shoggoth Monoliths are said to be capable of draining it.
entries.necronomicon.text.rituals.7: Some rituals require a living sacrifice. This means you need to have an adult animal within close proximity of the altar and pedestals. When the ritual starts, the target animal will begin to glow, and needs to die before the ritual ends. Failing to complete a ritual will trigger a Disruption, which is bad.
entries.necronomicon.text.pe.1: Potential Energy (PE) is a new form of energy presented in AbyssalCraft. It originates from a higher plane of existence (where no mortal has wandered), and can only be collected by tapping into Ley Lines using various methods. There exist objects capable of doing so, which will be explained here.
entries.necronomicon.text.pe.2: A good place to start obtaining materials required to create some of the PE collecting objects is Shoggoth Lairs, found in swamps and rivers.
entries.necronomicon.text.pe.3: Shoggoth Monoliths are also constructed with Monolith Stone (hence the name), while having statues placed on them. These statues can collect PE.
entries.necronomicon.text.pe.4: It should be noted that the Lesser Shoggoths only build these monoliths under certain conditions. Theorists claim it has to do with power positions (but they're genderless, and don't understand the concept of hieracrchy). If 6 (or more) Lesser Shoggoths are within 32 blocks of each other, one is prone to rise a monolith out of the ooze.
entries.necronomicon.text.pe.5: You should take into account that the Lesser Shoggoths have no limit on how many monoliths they construct, leading to a possible infestation.
entries.necronomicon.text.pe.6: If you notice Shoggoth activity near your homestead, it is highly advised that you immediately evacuate your land, or construct a large wall (or other defensive measures) to ensure the infestation doesn't spread onto your land. Recovering your land from a Shoggoth infestation is quite difficult, so be cautious.
entries.necronomicon.text.pe.7: The statues come in different shapes, all depicting Great Old Ones. They can transport PE to nearby players holding Necronomicons when under open sky.
entries.necronomicon.text.pe.8: It should be noted that you harvesting PE isn't appreciated. This causes disruptions to occur (displayed by a bolt of lightning striking the statue, or other PE manipulator). Disruptions are random events that can affect the player, other entities or the environment. Their purpose is to punish those who tries to drain PE from the higher plane.
entries.necronomicon.text.pe.9: Statues have a limited PE transfer range to nearby collectors. Collectors need to be placed in the yellow frame (with a two block gap between it and the statue).
entries.necronomicon.text.pe.10: When placed on Monolith Stone Pillar Blocks, the statues range can be increased up to two blocks. Statues on pillars can transfer energy to Collectors further down.
entries.necronomicon.text.pe.11: An Energy Depositioner is another PE manipulator. It works like a generator, where the "fuel" are Stone Tablets charged with PE.
entries.necronomicon.text.pe.12: One way to boost the efficiency of statues (and other PE manipulators) is through the use of Ritual Charms. They can boost various stats (check the tooltip).
entries.necronomicon.text.pe.13: You can also craft an Energy Pedestal, which can collect PE from statues (and other PE manipulators). Items that can hold PE can be placed on the pedestal to charge.
entries.necronomicon.text.pe.14: Along with the Energy Pedestal there's the Sacrificial Altar, which can convert life-force from dying mobs into PE (targeted mobs glow).
entries.necronomicon.text.pe.15: Another way to collect PE from manipulators is with an Energy Collector. It works like an Energy Pedestal (except you can't place items on it).
entries.necronomicon.text.pe.16: Energy Relays are used to transfer PE, and can do so in any direction (but it can't transport it through solid blocks, except glass).
entries.necronomicon.text.pe.17: Building networks with Energy Relays allows you to transport PE over larger distances. Energy Relays can drain PE from PE Collector placed next to it.
entries.necronomicon.text.pe.18: In order to store greater amounts of PE, you can create an Energy Container. They allow insertion through Energy Relays or interaction with the block.
entries.necronomicon.text.pe.19: If the PE production still is too slow, you can also upgrade the various PE handling blocks through infusion rituals to boost stats.
entries.necronomicon.text.pe.20: Upon reaching Omothol, you will be able to create deity-specific Ritual Charms (with an Abyssalnomicon), or buy them from Remnant Priests. Those charms will give an additional boost if used on manipulators associated with the same deity as the one displayed on the charm.
entries.necronomicon.text.machines.info: Check the information section for information regarding the different machines, or the other sections for all recipes for the specified machine. The recipes aren't sorted in any way.
entries.necronomicon.text.machines.1: The Transmutator is used to transmute objects into other objects, which can revert a process or simply convert an object into it's opposite. It's fueled by any Coralium materials, Coralium-plagued Flesh and any Crystallized element (full crystal or shard).
entries.necronomicon.text.machines.2: The Crystallizer is used to crystallize elements, isolating the base elements (or molecules) they're made from. It's fueled by any Dreaded material, Dread Fragments and any Crystallized element (full crystal or shard).
entries.necronomicon.text.machines.3: The Engraver is used to engrave coins, allowing you to trade things with Remnant. The "fuel" used in engraving is engraving templates, that wear out after a certain amount of uses. If you want to re-engrave a coin, you have to use a blank engraving on it first (to un-engrave it).
entries.necronomicon.text.machines.4: The Materializer is used to create objects by combining base elements (obtained through crystallization). The Materializer uses no fuel, but requires a Necronomicon to function, and a Crystal Bag with crystals to materialize objects from.
entries.necronomicon.text.knowledge.1: Some information in this book is incomprehensible to your puny, regular, untwisted mortal mind. By studying artifacts, listening to the whispers from statues, defeat monsters and explore the surroundings, you can expand your mind with new knowledge, enabling you to comprehend the information. Some Items and Blocks also require knowledge in order to be comprehended.
entries.necronomicon.text.knowledge.2: Treasure chests can contain lost pages with information, and in old structures scattered about, you can uncover murals that will grant you knowledge. Statues depicting Great Old Ones can sometimes be heard whispering things. Through combat you can gain knowledge of the enemy after defeating it. Exploring biomes and dimensions will grant you new knowledge.
entries.necronomicon.text.knowledge.3: Information you can't comprehend appears in Aklo glyphs rather than the human alphabet. The following page has an example of such glyphs:
entries.necronomicon.text.coraliumplague.1: The Coralium Plague is a disease originating from the Abyssal Wasteland. It's capable of transforming infected victims on death into stronger monsters. It's only considered a plague by those harmed by it.
entries.necronomicon.text.coraliumplague.2: An antidote for the Coralium Plague can be made with a Water Bottle, a Wasteland's Thorn, a piece of Anti-Plagued Flesh and a piece of Abyssal Shoggoth Flesh.
entries.necronomicon.text.dreadplague.1: The Dread Plague is a disease originating from the Dreadlands. It's a very infectious disease, swiftly travelling between hosts, but also transforming the ground around those afflicted by it, thus allowing the plague to grow stronger. The only place known to be completely immune to the Dread Plague is Omothol.
entries.necronomicon.text.dreadplague.2: An antidote for the Dread Plague can be made with a Water Bottle, a Dreadlands Sapling, a Dread Fragment and a piece of Dreaded Shoggoth Flesh.
entries.necronomicon.text.placesofpower.info: Structures of devotion appeasing the Great Old Ones, allowing for safe PE generation.
entries.necronomicon.text.placesofpower.1: Places of Power are shrine-like structures built to show devotion to the Great Old Ones. These sites of worship spread the word of the Great Old Ones, while also enabling harvesting of PE without disruptions. Along with the safe retrieval of energy, these structures can also boost various stats of the statues contained in them.
entries.necronomicon.text.placesofpower.2: In the structures section you can view the structures you've gained knowledge on how to build, their dimensions and what stats they amplify (if any). The point where you form the structure (by sneak right-clicking it with your Necronomicon) will change block in the preview to indicate where it is. Hovering over the preview shows a list of blocks used to build it.
entries.necronomicon.text.spells.info: Check the information section for information regarding spells, or the compendium for available spells.
entries.necronomicon.text.spells.1: In order to get started with spells you need to obtain some scrolls to inscribe the spells onto. Most of the available scrolls (except the greater) can be created through rituals or bought from Remnants. Spells in the compendium show which scroll they require (if the center slot is empty you can use any scroll).
entries.necronomicon.text.spells.2: Currently the quality of the scroll used has no impact on the inscribed spell, but in a future update some aspects of a spell will improve depending on which scroll you use. The unique scrolls will likely do something beyond that.
entries.necronomicon.text.spells.3: Spellcasting is done by right-clicking while holding an inscribed scroll (you also need an item that holds PE in your inventory for the casting to tap into). If the spell type is "Charging", you need to hold down the mouse button for 3 seconds, otherwise it's instant. Depending on the spell, you might need to target something specific while casting.
entries.necronomicon.text.itemtransportsystem.1: Spirit Tablet Shards can either be bought from Remnants or found as loot in buildings throughout Omothol. In a ritual involving 4 pieces and a Life Crystal, you can create a Spirit Tablet.
entries.necronomicon.text.itemtransportsystem.2: The Spirit Tablet is a tool allowing you to move Items by having spirits possess them. The tablet comes with a bunch of keybindings used to switch modes, open the filter inventory, clear the current set path. The modes include one for setting paths, one for applying configurations and one for clearing them.
entries.necronomicon.text.itemtransportsystem.3: The "Set Path" mode allows you to create a route for the items to move by right-clicking with the tablet on the ground. Sneak right-click on the desination block.
entries.necronomicon.text.itemtransportsystem.4: You don't necessarily have to lay out a route if you don't want to, only selecting the destination block also works just fine. When the Spirit Tablet is in the "Set Path" mode, the selected path will display as a line of redstone particles (where the last selected position consist of green particles). The path can be cleared using a keybind (check the tooltip of the item).
entries.necronomicon.text.itemtransportsystem.5: With a keybind (check the item tooltip), you can open an inventory to set a filter, which support up to 5 Items, subtypes (a Block of Stone would also filter for Andesite, Granite, etc), NBT (a piece of enchanted armor would only allow for other pieces of enchanted armor). The filter is optional, and if not set anything is accepted.
entries.necronomicon.text.itemtransportsystem.6: When you're in the "Apply Configuration" mode, sneak right-click on the block you wish to transport items from. Side matters, so keep that in mind if the block only extracts from one side.
entries.necronomicon.text.itemtransportsystem.7: When you're in the "Remove Configuration" mode, you can remove all applied configurations from a block by sneak right-clicking them. Breaking and placing the block would do the same thing, but this saves you time in comparison.
entries.necronomicon.text.itemtransportsystem.8: There are two utility spells (named "Display Routes" and "Toll The Bell") which can aid you in keeping track of defined routes, and also starting/stopping them. "Display Routes" will reveal any active routes in your vicinity, and "Toll The Bell" will start or stop routes from the block you're looking at (or all nearby if not targeting one).
